question: Initially $10\text{ cm}^3$ of nitrogen and $24\text{ cm}^3$ of hydrogen are mixed in a container. The temperature and pressure remain constant. Calculate the volume of gas that will remain in the container after the reaction is completed.
memo:
$V(\text{N}_2) : V(\text{H}_2) : V(\text{NH}_3) = 1 : 3 : 2$
$V(\text{N}_2\text{ reacted}) = \frac{1}{3} V(\text{H}_2) = \frac{1}{3}(24) \checkmark = 8\text{ dm}^3$
Volume $\text{N}_2$ remains $= 10 - 8 \checkmark = 2\text{ dm}^3$
Volume of gas that remains $= 2 + 16 \checkmark = 18\text{ dm}^3\text{ gas} \checkmark$
